notes: Found a bunch of rounded quartzite cobbles along the gravel bar. Some had really nice pink and white banding. The river was running pretty low which made it easy to walk around. Will definitely come back in the fall.

Hiking up the canyon I spotted several chunks of petrified wood eroding out of the mudstone slopes. Most pieces were small but one was about the size of a cantaloupe and still showed the original wood grain really clearly. Didn't take anything since I'm not sure about collecting rules here.

Small obsidian flakes scattered along the river bank near a volcanic formation upstream. Nothing huge but the glassy black surfaces were unmistakable. Brought home three small pieces. Water was a bit high from snowmelt.

locationName: Provo River Delta - Utah Lake Shore
notes: Lots of chert nodules and flint-like material washing up on the lakeshore near the river mouth. Some pieces show clear conchoidal fracture. Also found a few interesting fossils embedded in limestone cobbles. Good spot for an afternoon walk.

The metamorphic rock exposures along the Eagle River here are incredible. Found several small red garnets weathering out of biotite schist on the canyon walls. The garnets are pretty small but well formed dodecahedra shapes. Great access from the highway pullout.

Tried gold panning for the first time at the public panning area on Clear Creek. Got a few tiny flakes after about two hours - not enough to retire on but really fun. The creek has tons of nice metamorphic cobbles too. Very crowded on weekends.

The Sangre de Cristo mountains deliver some beautiful metamorphic material down the Rio Hondo. Found sheets of muscovite mica that catch the light really nicely. Also spotted some pegmatite blocks with large feldspar crystals. Elevation here is high so it got cold fast in the afternoon.

Pulled off at the rest area in the gorge and spent an hour looking at the exposed limestone cliffs right there. Found some nice brachiopod and crinoid fossils in loose talus at the base of the cliff. Nothing to collect but great for photos. The red and gray layered canyon walls are stunning.

Oregon thunderegg and agate country! Walked the BLM road along the John Day and found several agate nodules in the rhyolite. Cracked one open and it had nice clear chalcedony inside with some purple tinting - maybe amethystine? Will bring tools to break them open next time.

Idaho is one of the only places on earth to find star garnets. Spent the day digging in the gravel deposits near the river. Found three small garnets, only one shows a faint star when you hold it to bright light. Really cool experience. Bug spray is absolutely mandatory up here.

Montana yogo sapphires are world famous but the alluvial deposits in the Stillwater drainage have some nice material too. Scooped gravel from a low bar and panned it out. Found two tiny blue stones that could be sapphires - need to take them to a gem shop to confirm. Amazing scenery.

The canyon walls expose some of the oldest rocks in Wyoming. Drove the highway through and stopped at several pullouts. Found petrified wood fragments on a slope near the north end of the canyon. The colors ranged from brown to reddish orange. No large pieces, just scattered chunks.

Northern California gold country! Hiked down to the Scott River gravel bar and spent an afternoon panning. Got a tiny amount of flour gold and one small picker. The river was clear and the swimming holes here are incredible. Saw a black bear on the drive in.

locationName: Agua Fria River below Lake Pleasant
notes: The Agua Fria valley is classic Apache Tears territory. Found dozens of small rounded obsidian nodules in the gravelly soil around the river terraces. When you hold them up to sunlight they're a beautiful translucent smoky brown. Super easy collecting, just walk and look down.

Copper country! The Gila River drainage runs through old copper mining district and the turquoise-green chrysocolla is everywhere in the float rocks. Found a nice piece about the size of my fist with bright blue-green color coating the matrix. Also spotted malachite on a few pieces.

Nevada is known for Virgin Valley fire opals and the Humboldt drainage can produce some nice common opal too. Found a few pieces of potch opal in white and light blue. No gem quality but the geology here is interesting - volcanic tuffs everywhere. Very flat and hot, bring lots of water.

The upper Yakima gravel bars have nice chalcedony and carnelian material. Found several orange-red carnelian pieces ranging from marble-sized to fist-sized. One piece has really nice translucency. The river was running fast from a recent rain so I stayed on the upper bars.

The Llano Uplift is Texas Hill Country granite country. The river runs right over exposed pink granite bedrock in places. Collected some interesting float including a piece with large pink orthoclase phenocrysts. The swimming hole near the ford was irresistible on a 95-degree day.

The Frio runs through thick Edwards Limestone and there are fossils everywhere. Found oyster shells, echinoids (sea urchins), and some interesting coiled ammonites in the loose gravel. The water is bright blue-green and crystal clear. One of my favorite rivers in Texas.

Mississippi petrified wood is some of the best I've ever seen. The Pearl River system has carried material from ancient forests and the wood structure is perfectly preserved in many pieces. Found a log section about 18 inches long with bark texture still visible. Left it - too heavy to carry out.

The Pennsylvanian sandstone and shale here produces some interesting iron concretions. Found several spherical ones and a few that look like tiny discs. The fall colors were just starting to turn and the gorge views from the rim are absolutely worth the drive.

Found aragonite and calcite material in the talus below some limestone bluffs along the Green River. Nothing like cave formations, just surface float, but the crystalline structure is nice. The river here is incredibly scenic and there were great blue herons everywhere.

Finally made it to the UP of Michigan! Spent the day walking the Lake Superior beach near the river mouth. Found three Lake Superior agates - small but with the classic iron-banded red and yellow chalcedony bands. Also found several pieces of prehnite and greenstone. Cold and windy but totally worth it.

New Hampshire is called the Granite State for good reason. The Ammonoosuc drainage picks up material from pegmatite veins in the White Mountains. Found several smoky quartz crystals - one is a nice doubly-terminated crystal about 2 inches long. Fall foliage was absolutely spectacular.

Maine is world famous for its tourmaline pegmatites and the Androscoggin drainage picks up fragments from the Oxford County gem pegmatites upstream. Found a small piece of black schorl tourmaline and what looks like a bit of green elbaite. The mill town of Rumford has a huge waterfall right downtown too.
